newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may expand Eurobonds to other cities - aide.
newsitem.headline: Russia may expand Eurobonds to other cities - aide.

text.p: A presidential decree setting terms on three Russian regional Eurobond offerings may be expanded to include other regions, a government press official said late on Saturday.
Andrei Pershin, spokesman for First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov, said only the cities of Moscow, St Petersburg and Nizhny Novgorod region had met the requirements to issue Eurobonds so far.
But he said other cities or regions earning such ratings would also be allowed to issue bonds, although the procedure by which they would receive permission was not clear.

According to a presidential decree this week, the total debt issue by Moscow, St Petersburg and Nizhny Novgorod would be limited to 30 percent of their revenues, excluding loans. There would be limits on total debt service charges to 15 percent of non-debt revenues.

The local governments must also obtain two international credit ratings and get permission from the Russian Central Bank before they can issue the bonds, which would be subject to double-taxation treaties, the Kremlin said.

Other regions considering or planning Eurobonds include the Republic of Tatarstan in central European Russia, and the regions of Irkutsk in Siberia, Sverdlovsk in the Urals and Leningrad surrounding St Petersburg.
Pershin said the Ministries of Economy, Finance and other ministries would draw on the experience of the first three regional Eurobond issues in drafting further legislation on such issues.
